clue.text: Fish and Turkey not popular

parts.note: TR is the international code for Turkey
out of fashion, no longer in favour

explanation.surface: A menu choice: fish and turkey, but the turkey is not a popular dish.
explanation.definitionFit: A trout is a freshwater game fish of the salmon family.

clue.text: Well-built for cycling in symbolic adornments

indicators.note: cycling turns letters round like a wheel, so the first letter moves to the end

parts.note: strapping means big and strong

explanation.surface: A muscular cyclist wears ceremonial regalia for the ride.
explanation.definitionFit: Trappings are the outward signs or ornaments that go with a status or office.

clue.text: Swimmer in earthenware factory stripped

indicators.note: stripping something takes off its outer layer, so the first and last letters go

parts.note: a pottery is a workshop making earthenware

explanation.surface: Someone goes for a dip at the pottery works with no clothes on.
explanation.definitionFit: An otter is a river mammal that spends much of its time swimming.

clue.text: On top of everything, money invested in area of land returned

indicators.note: money invested in something is put inside it
something returned goes back the way it came, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: a lot is a plot of land
capital is money for investment

explanation.surface: To crown it all, cash put into a plot of land comes back.
explanation.definitionFit: To cap it all is an idiom meaning as a final addition, on top of everything else.

clue.text: Have role in what naughty siblings might be forced to do?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: take a role, as an actor does, or contribute

definitions.text: what naughty siblings might be forced to do?
definitions.meaning: second meaning, read literally: squabbling children are made to amuse themselves separately

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the last word: children kept away from each other play 'apart'. The question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: To play a part is the idiom for having a role or being involved in something.

clue.text: Perhaps insulin for juvenile delivered

parts.note: pro means in favour of

indicators.note: a speech is delivered out loud, so the word is judged by its sound

parts.note: a teen is a young person

explanation.surface: A diabetic youngster's insulin arrives by delivery.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half of the answer is pronounced like teen, a young person.
explanation.definitionFit: Insulin is a hormone made of amino acid chains, one example of a protein.

clue.text: To state the duration of life could be mean

parts.note: to aver is to declare or state
one's age is how long one has lived

explanation.surface: Telling someone how old they are might be unkind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mean' reads as unkind; it is the statistical sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The mean is the arithmetic average of a set of numbers.

clue.text: President Biden essentially retired

parts.note: Abe is Abraham Lincoln, the US president

indicators.note: the essence of a word is at its centre, so its middle letter is kept

parts.note: the middle letter of this five-letter name

explanation.surface: The US president has, at heart, stepped down.
explanation.walkthrough: Retired is the bedtime sense, not leaving office.
explanation.definitionFit: To retire can mean to go to bed, and abed means in bed.

clue.text: Dicky put eraser in holes

indicators.note: dicky is British slang for faulty or unsound, so the letters are out of order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone called Dicky pushes a rubber into the holes.
explanation.walkthrough: Dicky looks like a name; it is the British word for wobbly or faulty.
explanation.definitionFit: Apertures are openings or gaps, another word for holes.

clue.text: Leaves while in audition

indicators.note: an audition is a hearing, so the word is chosen by what it sounds like

parts.note: a while is a period of time

explanation.surface: An actor walks out during an audition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' looks like a verb, someone departing; it is the plural noun for foliage.
explanation.definitionFit: Thyme is a herb whose small aromatic leaves are used in cooking.

clue.text: Man receiving fine follows core characters from Partick Thistle

indicators.note: the core of a word is its middle, so only the central letters of the Scottish place name are kept

parts.note: the inside of Partick, dropping its first and last letters

indicators.note: a man receiving something holds it, so one word goes inside another

parts.note: he is a male pronoun
OK means all right, fine

explanation.surface: A football report: a player receiving a fine trails behind the key men of Partick Thistle, the Glasgow club.
explanation.walkthrough: Partick Thistle is a Glasgow football club, so 'Thistle' looks glued to its name; it is the definition. 'Follows' puts the man with OK inside after the core of Partick.
explanation.definitionFit: The globe artichoke is a cultivated plant of the thistle family grown for its edible flower head.

clue.text: European, on play's conclusion, creates lament

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for European
in cricket the on side is also called the leg side

indicators.note: the conclusion of a word is its final letter, so only the end of that word is used

parts.note: the final letter of play

explanation.surface: A European writer, after the last act of a play, produces a lament.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the on side and the leg side are the same half of the field, so 'on' can give LEG.
explanation.definitionFit: An elegy is a mournful poem, a lament for the dead.

clue.text: It might lie on one's head?

definitions.text: It might lie on one's head?

parts.words: It might lie on one's head?
parts.note: surface reading: something resting on top of a person, or a person telling a fib about themselves; setter's reading: in rhyming slang a falsehood is a pork pie, so a 'lie' worn on the head is a kind of hat with a flat crown

explanation.walkthrough: In Cockney rhyming slang 'porky pies' or 'pork pies' means lies. The answer is a flat-topped hat with a turned-up brim, so the 'lie' sits on the head.
explanation.definitionFit: This hat is named for its shape, like a pork pie, and slang makes that pie a fib.

clue.text: Large shed in fashion; it's an eyesore?

indicators.note: to shed something is to cast it off, so a letter is dropped

parts.note: style is fashion
L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: Someone discards an oversized garment in fashion, deciding it is an eyesore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Large shed in fashion' means the L is removed from STYLE. The question mark marks the definition as a pun: a stye is literally a sore on the eye.
explanation.definitionFit: A stye is an inflamed swelling on the eyelid, so it is quite literally a sore of the eye.

clue.text: Dead centre of fresh lesion around cut

indicators.note: one thing around another encloses it
a fresh version is a new one, so the letters are made over

parts.note: taken as written
to crop is to cut short

explanation.surface: A medical note: at the very middle of a new sore lies a gash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dead centre' reads as the exact middle; it is a centre for the dead.
explanation.definitionFit: A necropolis is a large ancient cemetery, literally a city of the dead.

clue.text: Organisms floating on water found in north London station

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for north
Euston is a main-line railway terminus in London

explanation.surface: Something living on a puddle turns up at a station in north London.
explanation.walkthrough: EUSTON is a London railway terminus. 'Found in' is a link here, not a signal to put one piece inside another.
explanation.definitionFit: Neuston is the biological term for tiny creatures living on or just under the surface film of water.

clue.text: Led nature rambles without modification

indicators.note: rambling wanders aimlessly, so the letters stray from their order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A guide led nature walks along the usual route without change.
explanation.definitionFit: Unaltered describes something left as it was, with no change made.

clue.text: Very tender, poop regularly, resulting in tear once?

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every second letter is taken

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth letters and so on of these three words

explanation.surface: A sore-bottomed baby's nappy change ends in tears.
explanation.walkthrough: Poop here is just letters to sample. 'Once' marks an archaic use: an eye-drop was an old word for a tear.
explanation.definitionFit: Eye-drop is an old poetic term for a teardrop, one drop falling from the eye.

clue.text: Stop entertaining naked walk becoming accepted

indicators.note: to entertain a guest is to have them inside, so one word holds another

parts.note: to prevent is to stop

indicators.note: naked means stripped of covering, so the outer letters go and the inside stays

parts.note: the inner letters of walk

explanation.surface: Police halt a streaker, and nude strolling becomes normal.
explanation.definitionFit: Something prevalent is widespread and generally current, so commonly accepted.

clue.text: Photograph contains every vegetable

indicators.note: one word containing another holds it within its own letters

parts.note: a shot is a photograph
all and every both mean the whole lot

explanation.surface: A still life: the photo shows every vegetable in the market.
explanation.definitionFit: A shallot is a small onion-like bulb used as a vegetable in cooking.

clue.text: Delight about river becoming stream

indicators.note: about means around, so one word is placed round the other

parts.note: to tickle is to amuse or delight
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: The joy of a river narrowing down into a brook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stream' looks like a noun after 'river'; it is a verb, to flow.
explanation.definitionFit: To trickle is to flow in a thin, slow stream.

clue.text: Flag-wearing idiot displaying device on organ

indicators.note: something wearing a garment has it wrapped round it, so one word goes around the other

parts.note: to flag is to tire, to grow weary
an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: A fool draped in a national flag puts on a show at the organ.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen makes 'Flag-wearing' look like one describing word, but flag is the verb meaning tire, wrapped around the idiot.
explanation.definitionFit: A tirasse is the coupler on an organ that links the pedals to a manual keyboard.

clue.text: Wrapper from can of unopened fuel

indicators.note: something not yet opened lacks its opening, so the first letter is dropped

parts.note: a tin is a can
taken as written
oil is a fuel

explanation.surface: Wrapping taken off a sealed fuel can.
explanation.definitionFit: Tinfoil is thin metal sheet used for wrapping food, a kitchen wrapper.

clue.text: Greek character to help with Austria retreating completely

indicators.note: retreating all the way means going right to the back, so the leading letter moves to the end

parts.note: to abet is to help, usually in wrongdoing
A is the international code for Austria: this names the first letter of the helping word, the one that moves

explanation.surface: A Greek letter lends a hand while Austria pulls out of the alliance altogether.
explanation.walkthrough: The A of ABET stands for Austria; it goes all the way to the back of the word rather than the word being reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: Beta is the second letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Analysis about revolutionary hosting platform

indicators.note: a revolution turns things round, so the letters run backwards
hosting means holding as a guest, so the letters sit inside the neighbouring words

parts.note: the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: A study of a radical figure who gave a platform to others.
explanation.definitionFit: A basis is a foundation or footing, a platform on which something is built.

clue.text: Soldiers criticise American lawyer, a playful individual

parts.note: two kinds of soldier: GI, an American soldier, and ANT, as in soldier ant
to pan is to criticise harshly
a DA is a district attorney in the US

explanation.surface: Troops attack a US attorney, who is a bit of a joker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soldiers' supplies two separate soldiers, GI and ANT.
explanation.definitionFit: Giant pandas are famous for clumsy, rolling play, so one is a playful creature.

clue.text: Reminder: head of night shift is starting late

indicators.note: a word starting late misses its beginning, so its first letter goes
the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the opening letter of night
to budge is to shift slightly

explanation.surface: A memo: the night-shift supervisor keeps clocking on late.
explanation.definitionFit: A nudge is a gentle prompt that jogs someone's memory.

clue.text: Sweet Caroline's introduction cut

indicators.note: an introduction comes first, so only the opening letter is used

parts.note: the first letter of the name
to hew is to cut with an axe

explanation.surface: The opening of the song Sweet Caroline gets cut short.
explanation.walkthrough: Sweet Caroline is the Neil Diamond song, but 'Sweet' is the definition. A chew is a chewy British sweet, a soft toffee-like candy.
explanation.definitionFit: A chew is a soft chewy confectionery, a type of sweet or candy.

clue.text: Son Hector, losing heart, turns red

indicators.note: turning round puts everything back to front
the heart of a word is its central letter, and losing it means that letter goes

parts.note: to hector is to harass or harry
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: Hector's son, his courage gone, blushes and turns red.
explanation.walkthrough: Hector looks like a name, but it is the verb, giving HARRY; its middle R goes, and with the son it is all read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Syrah is a red grape variety and the red wine made from it, also called Shiraz.

clue.text: Ken King, new member of parliament, meets creep

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
N is the abbreviation for new
a group of owls is called a parliament
to edge is to move slowly, to creep

explanation.surface: A man called Ken King, newly elected as an MP, meets a sycophant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Member of parliament' wants to be MP; here it is one bird from a parliament of owls.
explanation.definitionFit: Ken is a noun meaning range of understanding, as in 'beyond my ken'.

clue.text: Like a paddle steamer is, on reflection: with drops of water by hind part

indicators.note: a reflection is a mirror image, so the word is seen back to front

parts.note: taken as written and turned round
dew is droplets of water
the heel is the back of the foot

explanation.surface: A thoughtful look at a paddle steamer, spray dripping off its stern.
explanation.definitionFit: A side-wheel vessel has paddle wheels mounted on each side, as paddle steamers do.

clue.text: These pants can be made into coat

indicators.note: pants is British slang for rubbish, so the letters are poor and need rearranging

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A tailor says these trousers could be turned into a coat.
explanation.walkthrough: In British English pants are underpants and also slang for rubbish; the surface wants trousers.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheet of ice or paint is a thin layer, a coating spread over a surface.
